# Stand Firm in the Storm
## Scripture
"Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that in the Lord your labor is not in vain." – 1 Corinthians 15:58
## Reflection
Storms don't ask permission. They hit without warning—a job loss, a health scare, a family crisis. In those moments, a man's true foundation gets exposed. The question isn't whether the wind will blow, but whether you'll still be standing when it passes.

Paul's charge to the Corinthians is a warrior's command: be steadfast, immovable. That's not passive stubbornness—it's active resolve. It means planting your feet on the truth of the gospel and refusing to be shaken by circumstances. The resurrection Paul just finished describing is the bedrock. Because Christ rose, your labor has meaning. Because He lives, your faithfulness isn't wasted, even when you can't see the fruit yet.

Men, strength isn't the absence of pressure—it's what you do under it. Today, anchor yourself in the promises of God before the storm hits. Read His Word, pray with grit, and stand. The same power that raised Christ from the dead is at work in you. Don't drift. Don't fold. Stand firm.
## Daily Challenge
Hold a plank for 60 seconds and recite 1 Corinthians 15:58 aloud. Every second you hold, thank God for making you immovable in Him.
